correctness.rationale: For every odd q≥3, digit a and base b coprime to q, h≠0 and u∈H=<b> imply hau nonzero mod q, even when q is composite. The exact Fourier product ∏(1+ζ^{hau})=∏(1−ζ^{2hau})/(1−ζ^{hau}) equals 1 if 2∈H and equals (−1)^t ζ^(−haΣH) if −2∈H; each character block is thus a pure phase. Fourier inversion, including the zero mode 2^L, gives precisely the positive or signed shifted count recurrence. The integer constant follows from 2^t≡(−1)^t mod q in the negative case, and the repeated discrepancy is at most 2^{t−1} by reduction of any length mod t. Direct independent integer dynamic programming tested 68 recurrences for (q,b,a)=(7,3,1),(9,4,1),(11,3,1),(15,8,1),(7,4,3), including nontrivial negative shift S=3 mod9; the unrestricted identity rests on the character argument, not these finite tests.
